attribution.note: Marcus's own descriptive sentence in his signed post.

semantics.note: Faithful restatement of the four status descriptions. Each qualifier stays attached to the right person, including 'less than a year later' for Sutskever and 'at least until the end of the year' for Brockman.

contract.note: Reading Brockman's leave as the plan announced at publication is the ordinary reading of a present-tense status note. The September 2023 cover month is a reasonable reference point for Sutskever's timing.

evidence.note: OpenAI announcement of 14 May 2024: Sutskever is leaving. That is under a year after the September 2023 cover.
Reuters, Aug 2024: Brockman taking a sabbatical through year-end. Matches the leave plan as announced.
WIRED, same day: Murati resigned on 25 September 2024, so her departure was just announced.
Board announcement of Nov 2023 that Altman was removed.
OpenAI confirms Altman returned as CEO in Nov 2023.
Brockman came back in Nov 2024. That was after the post and does not change the leave plan announced when he wrote it.

reviews.rationale: Dated records support all four statuses as of 25 Sep 2024: Sutskever left in May 2024, Brockman was on an announced leave through year-end, Murati's resignation was announced that day, and Altman was fired and rehired in Nov 2023. Brockman's early return in November is context only, not a contradiction of the status he described.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his signed post.

semantics.note: Two separate observations, kept separate without any causal link added. 'No obvious moat' is an evaluative judgement with no stated measure.

contract.note: Reading 'moat' as a clear, durable competitive advantage and 'free' as no licence fee is ordinary. Whether a moat exists depends on a standard the speaker did not supply.

evidence.note: Meta's Llama 3.2 announcement presents its models as competitive with closed models. This is a company claim and supports only the 'similar software' part.
The Llama 3.2 licence grants royalty-free use, subject to some restrictions. Supports 'free'.
Llama 3.1 was released free in July 2024, before the target period. Background showing free distribution was ongoing.
OpenAI's o1-preview launch shows product differentiation. It is a company claim and does not establish a durable moat.

reviews.rationale: The evidence supports the Meta part: Llama models were comparable and royalty-free. Nothing in the packet shows whether OpenAI had a clear, durable advantage in September 2024, and the packet itself lists this as a gap. The support condition needs both parts, so the claim stays unresolved.

contract.note: Scoring only the three named departures and not the hedged count of others is fair to the speaker.

evidence.note: TechCrunch, Aug 2024: co-founder Schulman left for Anthropic.
TechCrunch, Feb 2024: Karpathy announced he had left OpenAI.
TIME profile from Sep 2024 says Leike left in May 2024.

reviews.rationale: Each named person had left OpenAI before the post on 25 Sep 2024: Karpathy in Feb, Leike in May and Schulman in Aug 2024. The hedged 'perhaps a dozen others' is not scored.
